title: Moses and the Shepherd
text:
In Rumi's poem, Moses was walking in the countryside when he heard a shepherd praying aloud. "O God, where are you, so that I can serve you? I would mend your shoes and comb your hair. I would wash your clothes and pick the lice from them. I would bring you milk, kiss your little hands and rub your little feet, and sweep your sleeping place at bedtime."

Moses was shocked. "Who are you talking to?" he demanded. "This is blasphemy! God has no need of shoes or milk. Stuff cotton in your mouth before your nonsense sets the world on fire." The shepherd was crushed. He tore his clothes, sighed, and wandered off into the desert.

Then a revelation came to Moses from God. "You have driven my servant away from me. You were sent to bring people close, not to cut them off. I have given each one his own way of praising me. I do not look at the words and the speech; I look at the heart and the inner state."

Moses ran into the desert, followed the shepherd's tracks and finally caught up with him. "Good news," he said. "You have permission. Say whatever your heart wants to say." But the shepherd answered that he had already moved beyond that place.
lesson: Do not mock or correct the way others express sincere feelings just because it is not your way. Look at the heart behind the words.
source: Jalal al-Din Rumi, Masnavi, Book II
